title: The Passover and the Plagues
reflectionText: Plague after plague fell, and still the king would not let Israel go. But on the last night, the people who were spared were not spared by their strength. They were spared by a lamb's blood struck on the door, and a word to stay inside until morning. When death passed through Egypt, what stood between a household and the cry outside was a mark they were told to make, and the waiting behind it.
editorialNotes: Text-First Story Factory 2.0 Batch B (journey backlog G1, approved 2026-07-23). Exodus 7-12, adult lane absent (kid 1907 covers the Passover). One coherent deliverance narrative across the six chapters, NOT a plague catalogue: the mounting confrontation, the Passover, the death of the firstborn, and the exodus. SHORT+FULL+LONG (WEB 408w/726w/1189w; KJV 441w/730w/1236w) — the ~4983-word source honestly sustains all three via scene selection and compression, not verse listing. HEART-HARDENING FIDELITY (owner requirement): each occurrence preserves exactly who hardens Pharaoh's heart — passive/self early (7:13, 7:22, 8:15, 8:19, 8:32 and the stubborn heart of 9:7) and Yahweh from the boils onward (9:12, 10:20, 10:27), with the self-hardening after the hail (9:34) kept as Pharaoh's own; the progression is not flattened to all-God or all-Pharaoh (verified across all lanes/lengths). Passover instructions (lamb, blood on the posts and lintel, unleavened bread, eaten in haste) and the death of the firstborn preserved with fidelity. No invented emotions inside Moses, Aaron, Pharaoh, the Israelites, or Egyptian families (Moses' 'hot anger' 11:8, Pharaoh's 'I have sinned' 9:27/10:16, the people's worship 12:27 are all source-stated). Boundary held inside Exodus 7-12; ends on the exodus from Rameses (12:37-42). KJV lane uses KJV diction (the Lord, lice, cattle, blains); WEB uses Yahweh. CODEX-AUDIT CORRECTION 2026-07-23: (F1) both SHORTS re-worked so the compressed heart-hardening no longer claims Yahweh was the agent of every hardening after the boils — the post-hail self-hardening (9:34, 'he and his servants') is preserved as Pharaoh's own before Yahweh resumes at the locusts and darkness; the reflections, figure-registry framing line, meta reflectionText, and all six manifest reflection copies were resynced to drop the flattened 'first Pharaoh, then Yahweh' claim. (F2) WEB full/long terminology corrected to the WEB extract: 'lightning that flashed down to the earth' (9:23, not the KJV 'fire ran along the ground') and 'firstborn of livestock' (11:5/12:29, not 'cattle'); KJV lane unchanged. Full/long heart-hardening progression was audited clean and is unchanged. Reflection recast to observation form (batch reflection-variety fix).
